name: Cyrus the Poet
bio: Cyrus the Poet is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to 6th century AD. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of the Cycle of Agathias, compiled in the sixth century AD.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the second volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book VII: 557).

poems.title: Book VII, 557
poems.author: Cyrus the Poet
poems.text: Mara had passed her thirtieth year and was approaching her thirty-third, when Hades cast at her his cruel dart and carried off the woman who was like a rosebud, a very counterpart of Penelope in her work.

poems.title: Book IX, 136
poems.author: Cyrus the Poet
poems.text: Would that my father had taught me to shepherd fleecy flocks, so that, sitting under the elms or piping under a rock, I might cheer my sorrows with music. Let us fly, ye Muses, from the stately city, and seek another home. I will announce to all that the pestilent drones have done mischief to the bees.

poems.title: Book IX, 623
poems.author: Cyrus the Poet
poems.text: Cypris with the Graces and her golden-arrowed boy bathed here and gave grace in payment.

poems.title: Book IX, 808: On the House of Maximinus
poems.author: Cyrus the Poet
poems.text: Maximinus built me in the newly constructed Rome, fixing my secure foundations actually on the beach. Infinite beauty extends itself around me. To right, left, and behind me lies the city, but facing me I see all the beauties of the Bithynian coast. At the foot of my most strong foundations the salt current rolls to the lovely sea, just touching the land in front of me enough to wet its edge. Often a man leaning out from me slightly has greatly rejoiced his heart, seeing in all directions different things : trees, houses, ships, sea, city, sky, and earth.

poems.title: Book IX, 809: On a Statue of Pindar
poems.author: Cyrus the Poet
poems.text: Cyrus set up Pindar beside the water, because singing to the lyre he said, “Water is best.”

poems.title: Book XV, 9: In Praise of the Emperor Theodosius
poems.author: Cyrus the Poet
poems.text: All the renowned deeds of Achilles are thine, except his secret love; thou drawest the bow like Teucer, but art no bastard; thou hast the illustrious beauty of Agamemnon, but wine does not disturb thy mind. In prudence I liken thee in every way to Odysseus, but thine is without evil fraud, and thou dost distil, O King, honeyed accents like those of the old man of Pylos, before thou seest Time touching the third generation.

poems.title: Book XV, 10
poems.author: Cyrus the Poet
poems.text: How is it we find martyrs in the deep sea? Tell me, ye rocks, tell me, ye long waves, with how many tempests they battled. The ship was broken, the mast fell, the keel sank, the cargo perished.
